10.1002_adma.75459: Pervasive contamination by micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) poses threats to environmental and human health; however, their sensitive detection is challenged by low concentrations and lack of effective enrichment methods. Herein, we present a plasmonic coacervate platform that spontaneously sequesters polystyrene (PS) MNPs from water while facilitating surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) detection. Coacervate microdroplets, formed through the liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) of cationic poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) and anionic adenosine triphosphate, exhibit a positive surface charge and a hydrophobic interior, enabling capture of nanoscale or microscale negatively charged PS MNPs with enrichment rates of 99.4% and 91.1%. The co‐encapsulation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) generates three‐dimensional droplet‐confined SERS hotspot networks, resulting in an enhancement factor of 2.72 × 10 9 , excellent uniformity, and minimum detectable concentration of 1 and 10 ng/mL for nano‐ and micro‐scale PS, demonstrating strong linear correlations. This platform achieves recoveries ranging from 87% to 108% for PS MNPs spiked into filtered tap and river water and successfully detects PS MNPs released from commercial plastic cups and expanded polystyrene containers under simulated daily use. Our work establishes a simple, rapid, and sensitive strategy that integrates spontaneous analyte sequestration with plasmonic amplification, thus offering a new avenue for monitoring MNPs and assessing the safety of food‐contact materials.
10.1002_smll.75087: Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising candidates for catalyzing the electrochemical CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) to alleviate environmental and energy issues. However, rationally designing active sites to enhance the adsorption of the key *CO intermediate for efficient CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ conversion remains a significant challenge. Herein, we propose a coordination atom regulating strategy to optimize the electronic structure of the Cu site for CO 2 RR. A Cu‐MOF ( JXUST‐304 ) featuring CuN 2 O 2 active site (originating from CuN 2 O 3 nodes removed of coordinated DMF) was constructed based on a ligand incorporating both pyridine N and ‐COOH groups. JXUST‐304 displays superior catalytic performance in the CO 2 ‐to‐C 2+ conversion with a Faraday efficiency of 64.7% alongside a partial current density of 129.1 mA cm −2 , surpassing similar Cu‐MOF with CuN 4 active sites. The unique N/O co‐coordination mode modulates the electronic structure to optimize the d‐band center of Cu sites, which enhances the adsorption of *CO intermediate. Meanwhile, 3d xz ‐2p z π back bonding interaction reduces the formation energy barrier for *CHO to facilitate C–C coupling, resulting in a selective increase in C 2+ products. This work offers insight into regulating the catalytic active sites within MOFs at the molecular level to promote the generation of targeted products.
10.1002_smll.76107: The large‐scale deployment of proton exchange membrane fuel cells is hindered by the intrinsic activity‐stability trade‐off in Pt‐based alloy catalysts, arising from transition metal dissolution and nanoparticle aggregation. Herein, we develop a mesh‐island confinement strategy to construct a ternary PtCoSn catalyst via alternating atomic layer deposition. In this design, Co preferentially occupies low‐coordination Pt sites, while Sn is selectively enriched on the nanoparticle surface and carbon support. Upon reduction, a PtCoSn alloy core is formed and stabilized by a surface SnO‐based mesh and support‐confined islands. This architecture enables the catalyst to achieve superior oxygen reduction reaction activity and significantly enhanced stability compared to conventional binary alloys by suppressing transition metal dissolution and inhibiting nanoparticle migration. The membrane electrode assembly achieves a peak power density of 1.46 W cm −2 and a mass activity of 0.73 A mg Pt −1 , with only 14.4% performance degradation after 30 000 accelerated durability cycles. This work establishes a general strategy for the rational construction of highly durable electrocatalysts through mesh‐island confinement.
10.1002_tcr.70263: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a major kinetic bottleneck in alkaline water electrolysis, motivating the development of efficient, durable, and cost-effective electrocatalysts. This review critically examines NiCo layered double hydroxides (NiCo-LDHs) as earth-abundant OER precatalysts, emphasizing how synthesis, structural modification, and operando reconstruction govern catalytic performance. Reported design strategies are evaluated according to the key limitations they address, including insufficient active-site accessibility, suboptimal intrinsic activity, poor electrical conductivity, restricted mass transport, uncontrolled reconstruction, and limited scalability. The crystal chemistry, interlayer structure, and anodically induced transformation of NiCo-LDHs into catalytically active Ni/Co oxyhydroxide-like phases are discussed as a basis for understanding structure-activity relationships. Major synthesis and modification approaches, including morphology control, heteroatom doping, defect engineering, conductive-support integration, interface engineering, and heterostructure formation, are critically compared in terms of activity, transport, durability, fabrication complexity, and structural stability. Particular emphasis is placed on post-OER, in situ, and operando characterization for identifying working-state structures. Finally, challenges in electrochemical benchmarking, metal dissolution, substrate effects, long-term stability, and scalable fabrication are assessed, providing design principles for advancing NiCo-LDH-based electrodes toward practical alkaline water electrolysis.
10.1016_j.electacta.2026.148256: Herein, we demonstrate the Ir growth on conductive carbon paper (CP) by Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) for the preparation of HER electrocatalysts with precise control over the Ir loading and morphology, from single atoms to nanoparticles. Importantly, ALD electrode fabrication circumvents intermediate nanoparticle synthesis, transfer, and binder application steps, required for conventional sample preparation methods, allowing single step fabrication process. The electrocatalytic activity of the resulting Ir/CP electrodes was assessed in alkaline media (KOH) towards HER by the systematic variation of the number of ALD cycles. The results suggested the electrocatalytic performance to be an interplay between different catalytic parameters including, electrochemically active surface area, turnover frequency and mass activity. In particular, the Ir/CP electrode decorated with 300 Ir cycles exhibited superior catalytic performance, namely, lowest overpotential (32.7 mV), Tafel slope (80.6 mV dec -1 ), and minimal charge transfer resistance (0.7 Ω). A stability test for 60 h revealed a partial surface oxidation and Ir aggregation, yet it did not affect significantly the catalytic performance (∼15 mV increase in overpotential value). Overall, we present the ALD fabrication of Ir/CP electrodes as an efficient and durable HER catalyst in alkaline media, demonstrating the potential of ALD for designing high performance binder-free electrodes.
10.1038_s41467-026-76539-8: The intrinsic trade-offs between high-rate capacitive processes and high-capacity redox reactions fundamentally limit advanced electrochemical energy storage. Here, we transcend this paradigm by introducing cavity-enabled supramolecular microreactors as a versatile platform for synergistic bromine capacitive-redox electrochemistry. These microreactors exhibit voltage-responsive dual functions, operating as a high-capacity ion-sequestration matrix at low voltages governed by their tailored electrostatic cavity landscape, and dynamically switching to an anchoring and conversion-promoting center at high voltages via spatially confined noncovalent interactions distinct from conventional bonding. Deployed in an aqueous zinc-bromine battery, this strategy delivers a specific capacity of 481.8 mAh g−1 at 0.83 A g−1 and retains 89.4% of its capacity after 1500 cycles at a specific current of 8.3 A g−1. Our work transcends the conventional material design philosophy, establishing a general approach for breaking the intrinsic limits of electrode materials through molecular-scale ion regulation. Aqueous zinc-bromine batteries face a trade-off between capacitive power and redox capacity. Here, authors design cavity enabled supramolecular that dynamically switch from ion storage at low voltages to polybromide stabilization at high voltages, delivering high capacity, power and cycling durability.
10.1039_d5ta06721a: A flexible PEO/LiTFSI/LZP interlayer on LATP via drop-solution improved interfacial kinetics and stability of the LATP pellet. This raised the CCD to 1.58 mA cm −2 and enabled stable Li/LFP all-solid-state battery cycling for 250 cycles at 0.5C.
